sourcedFrom: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN (UNKNOWN)
cleanIntro: The Red Label is Ruger's over-and-under, made in 12, 20 and 28 gauge, and this book also covers the Woodside. It opens with a top lever, and the safety on the top of the receiver doubles as the barrel selector: S is safe, T fires the top barrel first, B the bottom. Ruger's takedown is three pieces: the forearm, the barrels, and the receiver with the stock. That is all the takedown Ruger asks for routine cleaning, and it tells owners not to go further unless they are qualified in shotgun repair. Keep the choke tubes screwed in while you clean.

steps.title: Safety on S, top lever right, barrels down
steps.action: Point the muzzles somewhere safe and keep your fingers out of the trigger guard. Move the safety back to S, push the top lever all the way to the right and swing the barrels down to open the gun. Fired shells are thrown out, but live shells are only lifted a little: take every one out by hand. Opening the gun does not unload it.
steps.quote: You must remove live (unfired) cartridges manually!
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — To Unload, p.21
steps.warn: The selective ejector mechanism only ejects fired shells. It does not eject live ammunition.

steps.title: Look into both chambers
steps.action: With the gun open, look into the top chamber and the bottom chamber yourself and make sure both are empty. Put all the ammunition away from where you will clean. Then close the empty gun: Ruger's takedown takes the forearm off first and opens the gun again after.
steps.quote: Check both chambers to be sure that the gun is unloaded.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Disassembly Procedure, step 1, p.23

steps.title: Latch lever down, forearm tip down gently
steps.action: Pull the forearm latch lever down to unlatch the forearm. Then pull the tip of the forearm down away from the barrels, slowly, only until you feel slight resistance. Stop there. Ruger warns that forcing it past that point can break it.
steps.quote: Unlatch forearm by pulling down on latch lever.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Assembling the Shotgun, step 2a, p.16
steps.warn: APPLICATION OF EXCESSIVE FORCE AT THIS POINT CAN RESULT IN BREAKAGE.

steps.title: Forearm forward and off
steps.action: Keep the tip of the forearm held away from the barrels and pull the forearm toward the muzzles. It comes off the barrels in one piece, with the forend iron in it.
steps.quote: While holding forearm tip away from barrels, carefully pull forearm toward the muzzle and remove forearm from barrels.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Assembling the Shotgun, step 2c, p.16

steps.title: Top lever right, open, lift the barrels out
steps.action: Hold the stock by the pistol grip. Push the top lever all the way to the right and open the gun, swinging the muzzles down. With the forearm off, nothing holds the barrels on, so keep a hand on them: lift the rear of the barrels out of the receiver as the trunnions in the receiver come out of their recesses at the front of the monobloc.
steps.quote: Push the top lever all the way to the right and open the gun, pivoting the muzzle end of the barrels downward and lifting the barrel assembly out of the receiver
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Disassembly Procedure, step 3, p.23

steps.title: Forearm back onto the barrels
steps.action: Put the forearm back on the barrels so it is not lying loose: line up the forend latch hook under the lower barrel with the latch lever and snap the two together. It comes off again before the barrels go back on the receiver.
steps.quote: Replace the forend assembly onto the barrel assembly by aligning the forend latch hook with the forend latch lever and snapping together.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Disassembly Procedure, step 4, p.23

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: On the bench now: the barrels with the forearm on them, and the receiver with the stock. That is all the takedown Ruger's book gives for cleaning and maintenance. The stock stays on, and the trigger, safety and ejectors stay where they are.
steps.quote: This completes the takedown required for all normal cleaning and maintenance purposes.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Disassembly Procedure, p.23

steps.title: Solvent patches, then dry patches
steps.action: Leave the choke tubes screwed in. With a proper cleaning rod, run a patch wet with solvent through each bore several times, then run dry patches through until no residue is left. Ruger counts the chamber as part of the bore, so the chambers get the same treatment.
steps.quote: Using a proper cleaning rod, run a solvent-wetted patch through each bore several times. Then run dry patches through the bore to remove all traces of residue.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Care and Cleaning, step 2, p.24

steps.title: Brass brush only if the patches will not shift it
steps.action: If lead or plastic wad residue stays in a bore after patching, scrub that bore its full length with a brass-bristle brush wet with solvent. When the fouling has come loose, go back to solvent patches and then dry patches.
steps.quote: scrub the bore, full length, with a solvent-wetted brass-bristle brush
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Care and Cleaning, step 3, p.24

steps.title: Choke tubes stay in while you clean
steps.action: Do not take the choke tubes out to clean. Cleaning a barrel with its tube out pushes dirt and fouling into the choke threads, and then the tube will not go in properly. If a tube does come out, do not fire the gun until it is back in, fully and tightly bottomed with the choke wrench.
steps.quote: it is recommended that a set of choke inserts be kept correctly tightened into the barrel at all times, including storage and cleaning.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Installation of Screw-In Chokes, p.18
steps.warn: Never fire the shotgun without the screw-in choke inserts in place.

steps.title: A very light film of oil on the monobloc and receiver
steps.action: Wipe the polished surfaces of the monobloc, the ejectors, and the inside of the receiver where the monobloc rests, then give them a very light film of gun oil. These are the surfaces that slide against each other every time the gun opens and closes. A film is enough; more only collects dirt.
steps.quote: The polished surfaces of the monobloc, ejectors, and inside surfaces of the receiver where the monobloc rests should be coated with a very light film of lubricating oil.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Care and Cleaning, step 4, p.24

steps.title: Lubricate where the forend iron meets the receiver
steps.action: Lubricate the area where the forend iron bears on the receiver. Ruger asks for a stainless steel lubricant there. Do this at regular intervals, and every time the gun has been out in sand, dust, high humidity, condensation or water.
steps.quote: Lubricate contact area of forend iron and receiver with Stainless steel lubricant.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Care and Cleaning, Periodic Maintenance, p.24

steps.title: Sparingly oiled cloth outside, oily patch before storage
steps.action: After the gun is back together, wipe the outside metal with a cloth that has only a little oil on it. If the gun is going into storage, swab each bore with an oily patch. Before you shoot it again, run a dry patch through both bores: oil left in a bore can obstruct it.
steps.quote: Swab the bores with an oily patch before storing the gun. Do not apply excess oil.
steps.cite: INSTRUCTION MANUAL FOR 12, 20 & 28 GAUGE RUGER® OVER & UNDER SHOTGUNS (Red Label Model, Woodside Model) — UNKNOWN — Care and Cleaning, step 5, p.24
steps.warn: Firing a shotgun with oil, grease, or any other material even partially obstructing the bore may result in damage to the shotgun and serious injury to the shooter and those nearby.

deepAbsentReason: Ruger's book ends at the field strip: after the forearm and barrels come off it says this completes the takedown required for all normal cleaning and maintenance, and that the gun should not be further disassembled by persons unqualified in shotgun repair (Disassembly Procedure, printed p.23).

cleaning.name: BORES
tasks: Solvent patch through each bore several times, chambers included
Dry patches until no residue is left
Brass brush with solvent only for lead or plastic residue the patches leave
Never fire the shotgun without the choke tubes in place

cleaning.name: MONOBLOC & RECEIVER
tasks: Monobloc, ejectors and the receiver seat wiped clean
A very light film of oil on those polished surfaces
Stainless steel lubricant where the forend iron meets the receiver

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR & STORAGE
tasks: Outside metal wiped with a sparingly oiled cloth
Oily patch through the bores before storage
Dry patch through both bores before the gun is fired again

reassembly: Forearm off the barrels again: latch lever down, tip down only to slight resistance, then forward and off. Ruger says never attach the barrels to the receiver with the forearm on.
Hold the stock by the pistol grip with the top lever pushed open to the right.
Engage the trunnions in the receiver with the recesses at the front of the monobloc.
Before you close it, make sure the small lugs on the outside of the ejectors are in their slots inside the front of the receiver. If they are not, closing the gun damages the receiver.
Swing the muzzles up so the monobloc seats in the receiver. The barrels are locked when the top lever snaps back to centre.
Put the rear of the forend iron over the ends of the ejectors and swing the front of the forearm up until the latch lever catches the hook under the lower barrel and snaps locked.
fncheck: With both chambers empty and the muzzles pointed somewhere safe: close the gun and check it is securely locked, with the top lever fully back in its centred position. Open it and check the safety has moved itself back to S, with the S fully showing. With the safety on S, move the selector to T and to B and back, keeping your fingers out of the trigger guard. It should click firmly into each position. If the selector moves too easily or will not sit firmly in any position, Ruger says stop using the gun and send it to its Newport, New Hampshire service department. Check the forearm is latched tight to the barrels.
